messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: DNS resolution error surge detected from eu-west-1 probe fleet. Service: api.redwood.ai. 5xx rate (resolver failures) hitting 18% for last 5m, latency 90p +2s. Paging oncall.

emma (oncall): ack — looking. paging sre and networking. tagging @raj @lucas :rotating_light:

raj (sre): diving in — pulling resolver metrics and recent GeoDNS changes. grabbing dig traces now. can someone post the probe list?

cloud-nanny: probe snapshot (last 5m): eu-west-1: SERVFAIL 17.8%, NXDOMAIN 0.6%, median latency 420ms, 95p 2100ms. eu-central-1: healthy.

lucas (networking): saw Cloudflare status blips earlier — partial resolver degradation in EU region (reports from partners). Route53 health checks also show elevated latencies for some endpoints. Not sure if it's Cloudflare or an upstream resolver mesh.

emma (oncall): jamie, any customer tickets?

jamie (support): a few EU customers reporting timeouts and error pages for product search and embeddings calls; CS is triaging but several enterprise customers flagged.

sarah (product): need quick customer-impact summary and status page update if customers are impacted.

raj (sre): quick checks I ran:
```
# sample checks
dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai A
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai A
curl -sS https://probe-api.internal/resolve?host=api.redwood.ai\n```
Results: Cloudflare-based resolvers returning SERVFAIL from some EU-anycast points; Route53 looks responsive but our GeoDNS policy still has eu-west weights high so clients hit the affected resolvers.

lucas (networking): agreed — looks like resolver-level failures on CF anycast edges in eu-west; Route53 propagation shows some stale records in a subset of edge caches (TTL mismatch observed). I suspect a rapid policy change earlier today + backend reconciliation leading to cache churn.

emma (oncall): mitigation options?

raj (sre): options ordered by risk: 1) Shift GeoDNS weights to prefer eu-central (failover) to steer away from affected edges. 2) Lower TTL to 30s to speed propagation (but increases query load). 3) Add additional client-side resolver fallback: prioritize VPC resolver then public ones. 4) Emergency Cloudflare route purge / contact CF support.

lucas (networking): I'll prepare the Route53 weight update. recommend do a canary change (10% -> eu-central) then ramp. Also set TTL to 60s first.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created: geodns-weight-update by lucas. CI checks passed. Approvals: required from @raj.

raj (sre): approve — go for canary.

lucas (networking): executing canary now. applying:
```
# Route53 change (infra):
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west","Weight":90,"TTL":300,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"1.2.3.4"}]}}]}'
# then adjust eu-central weight -> +10
```

emma (oncall): lucas — confirm when canary done. monitor client hits and resolver error rate.

lucas (networking): canary applied at 3123456802. TTL change to 60s applied at 3123456810.

cloud-nanny: metric update: 3m after canary: eu-west SERVFAIL -> 11%, eu-central traffic +9%. overall error rate down from 18% -> 7%.

jamie (support): relaying update to customers: "We're aware of DNS-related errors affecting EU users; we're routing traffic to alternate region and working with providers. We'll update in 30m."

sarah (product): please post to status.redwood.ai and include estimated impact and mitigation steps.

emma (oncall): posting status update now.

deploy-bot: canary succeeded, change set id CS-99823, no regressions. Recommend ramp to 100% over 15m.

raj (sre): ramp approved. lucas, proceed to full shift. after ramp, we should keep TTL low for 10m then restore.

lucas (networking): ramping to 100% at 3123456860.

cloud-nanny: 5m after ramp: global error rate 1.2%, eu-west now 1.5%, latency back to baseline.

emma (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for now. continuing to monitor 30m.

jamie (support): CS = informed customers we mitigated and we're monitoring. No escalations pending.

lucas (networking): filing ticket with Cloudflare and AWS Route53 support — attaching dig traces and resolver logs. opening case IDs in infra board.

raj (sre): action items:
- Formal postmortem (owner: raj)
- Confirm CF/Route53 root cause and get SLA credit if applicable (owner: lucas)
- Add automated GeoDNS canary runbook and implement safety TTL limits (owner: emma)
- Update client-side resolver fallback docs for product teams (owner: sarah)

emma (oncall): preparing handoff to morning oncall at 3123456900. leaving notes and runbook link.

emma (oncall): HANDOFF: incident currently mitigated, watching for reversion. follow-up tasks in #infra-postmortems.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Incident set to "Mitigated". Create postmortem within 72h.

lucas (networking): final note: we reverted TTL to 300s at 3123456915 after observing stability. Will keep low TTL only during active mitigation windows to avoid query storms.

raj (sre): closing the active page but keeping an eye on DNS metrics for next 24h. postmortem ticket: PM-4312 created.

emma (oncall): thanks team — great quick moves. :thumbsup:

sarah (product): will draft customer communication for tomorrow once we have root cause.

jamie (support): closing related support threads as "resolved by routing change" unless new evidence.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: mitigated -> monitoring. total duration (alert->mitigated) ~8m.
